subject.title: fix(security): bound hashFileContentsSync in approval script operand reads

question: Should approval fingerprinting retain support for script operands above 8 MiB through bounded chunked hashing, or should OpenClaw intentionally deny all such operands?
rationale: The PR turns a memory-safety repair into a new externally observable approval policy, and the supplied evidence does not establish that 8 MiB is an accepted product limit.

options.title: Use bounded chunked hashing
options.body: Keep the OOM protection while preserving approval support for larger regular script files.

options.title: Adopt the 8 MiB policy
options.body: Accept the compatibility break and document the denial behavior, rationale, and operator recovery path.

recommendation.title: Use bounded chunked hashing
recommendation.body: Keep the OOM protection while preserving approval support for larger regular script files.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership history for this approval path was not established from the available read-only evidence.
